description: The memory layer for your projects - so you and your agents never forget. dizz remembers intent, conventions, guardrails, and code health, and serves it up through the CLI instead of a context file that went stale the day after you wrote it.
instructions: Treat `dizz context` and `dizz config show` output as ground truth over what you infer from reading code. Query state through the CLI instead of reading files or code cold.
Never read or write `.dizz/` files directly - always go through the dizz CLI. If a command fails, surface the failure instead of falling back to reading the files.

Capture durable project knowledge (conventions, decisions, guardrails) via `dizz config add-instruction`/`add-guardrail` and open work via `dizz intent add`. Long-lived intent belongs in intents, not inline TODO/FIXME comments.
Every write-back command (config/intent/guardrail add or resolve) requires explicit user approval before running, regardless of how small the change seems.
Before a large change, run `dizz snapshot --auto` and check the blast radius with `dizz graph query <entity> --depth 3`.
Write clean, idiomatic Go. Comments explain why, not what (non-obvious logic excepted). Prefer simplicity over cleverness.
Never ignore errors. Use `errors.Is`/`errors.As`; wrap with `fmt.Errorf("context: %w", err)`. Internal packages never call `log.Fatal` or `os.Exit` - return errors up to the cmd/ CLI layer.
No external dependencies beyond stdlib + cobra. A new dependency needs explicit justification.
Prefer interface design based on consumer needs (accept interfaces, return structs). Keep `main.go` and the cmd/ layer thin; put logic in internal packages.
Always pass `context.Context` first to I/O/blocking functions; manage goroutines via `errgroup.Group` with a clear termination path.

guardrails.reason: Immutable content-addressed state store; never hand-edit, mutate only via dizz CLI
Agent skill definitions are carefully maintained; changes ship via dizz releases
Dependency changes must be explicitly approved; dizz is intentionally stdlib + cobra only

severity_scale.1: Low - informational, no immediate action needed
